extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes two conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII.

For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometric identification systems), the provider may use internal control (if harmonised standards or common specifications were applied) or must use the notified body procedure under Annex VII if standards were not fully applied.

Annex VII (notified body assessment) is mandatory for biometric identification systems and certain high-risk AI systems embedded as safety components in products covered by Annex I (Section A) harmonisation legislation; most other high-risk AI systems may use the Annex VI self-assessment route.

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU product-safety legislation listed in Section A of Annex I (e.g., medical devices, machinery), the provider must follow the conformity assessment procedures of that sectoral legislation, with notified bodies additionally verifying compliance with the AI-specific requirements of the AI Act.

A new conformity assessment is required if a high-risk AI system is substantially modified, except where changes were predetermined by the provider at the time of the initial assessment and are part of information in the technical documentation (relevant to systems that continue to learn after deployment).

Under Article 43(1), for the purposes of the Annex VII conformity assessment, the provider may choose any notified body; however, where the high-risk AI system is intended to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities, or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies, the relevant market surveillance authority (under Article 74(8) or (9)) acts as the notified body instead.

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority to authorise, by derogation from Article 43, the placing on the market or putting into service of specific high-risk AI systems for a limited period, for exceptional reasons of public security, protection of life and health, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets, without the system having completed the standard conformity assessment.

Annex VII, point 4.5, provides that a notified body may, where necessary and after other reasonable means of verification are exhausted, be granted access to the training and trained models of the AI system, including relevant parameters, subject to Union IP and confidentiality protections.
Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes requirements for identification numbers and public lists of notified bodies designated under the AI Act.

As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing across Member States, limited capacity, and uncertain timelines ahead of the August 2026 deadline for high-risk AI obligations.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act for medical-device-related high-risk AI systems.

High-risk AI obligations, including the requirement for conformity assessment and CE marking, are described as fully applying from August 2026 (with one source citing August 2, 2026 as the compliance deadline for SaaS providers to issue declarations of conformity).

Post-2026, notified bodies designated under the AI Act are expected to begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments, with the intersection between these and existing MDR/IVDR notified body assessments for medical devices still being worked out.

The Council document (7322/26) describes a coding system (e.g., AIP 0101, AIP 0102) used to define the scope of designation of conformity assessment bodies notified under 'Article 30' of 'this Regulation,' tied to categories of AI systems under Annex I of the AI Act.

A Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836 / 2025/0359 (COD)) proposes creating a new Annex XIV listing notified and designated organisations for the AI Act within the Commission's NANDO information system, and separately proposes amendments to Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements into aviation safety regulation.

As of October 2025, the NANDO system lists 51 MDR-designated notified bodies and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies (under the separate Medical Devices Regulation and In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation framework, not the AI Act specifically).

Under the Cyber Resilience Act (a separate but related EU digital regulation), zero notified bodies had been designated in the Commission's NANDO database as of late June 2026, despite the notified-body rules starting to apply on 11 June 2026; a target of sufficient notified body capacity is set for 11 December 2026, with full application of the CRA from 11 December 2027.

The 2021 Commission proposal text of Article 43 (as of the original October 2021 proposal document) described the conformity assessment procedure for Annex III point 1 (biometric) systems in terms substantially similar to, but not identical to, the final adopted text.
A November 2022 Council compromise text of the proposed Article 43 described an evolving conformity assessment procedure for Annex III point 1 AI systems, prior to final adoption of the AI Act.

Under Article 43(5), the European Commission has the power to adopt delegated acts (per Article 97) to update Annex VI (internal control procedure) and Annex VII (QMS and technical documentation assessment) in light of technical progress, without needing to formally revise the AI Act itself.

report:
# Conformity Assessment for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act: Procedures and Notified Body Designation Status

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes a dual-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems: internal control (Annex VI) or notified body assessment (Annex VII), with the latter generally mandatory for biometric identification systems and products already subject to sectoral safety legislation (medium confidence). However, the notified body ecosystem required to implement Annex VII assessments appears largely undeveloped, with no source identifying specific organizations designated under the AI Act itself as of early-to-mid 2026, despite the approaching August 2026 deadline for high-risk obligations (low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 of the AI Act establishes two primary routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)). For biometric identification systems under Annex III point 1, providers may use internal control if harmonised standards or common specifications were applied, but must use the notified body procedure under Annex VII where standards were not fully applied (low confidence) ([EC Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf)). Interpretive sources suggest Annex VII is effectively mandatory for biometric systems and for high-risk AI embedded as safety components in products covered by Annex I Section A legislation, with most other high-risk systems eligible for Annex VI self-assessment (low confidence) ([Quantamix](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)).

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU product-safety legislation (e.g., medical devices, machinery) under Annex I Section A, providers must follow that sectoral legislation's conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI-specific compliance (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

### Procedural Details
A new conformity assessment is required after substantial modification, unless changes were predetermined and documented at initial assessment—relevant to continuously learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Under Article 43(1), providers may generally choose any notified body, except where systems are intended for use by law enforcement, immigration/asylum authorities, or EU institutions, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from standard assessment for limited periods on public security or health grounds (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Annex VII point 4.5 allows notified bodies access to training and trained models, including parameters, where necessary and subject to IP/confidentiality protections (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing across Member States and uncertain capacity ahead of the August 2026 deadline (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)). As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated for medical-device-related high-risk AI systems specifically (low confidence) ([AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)). A Council document (ST-7322-2026) describes a coding system (e.g., AIP 0101) for defining designation scope tied to Annex I categories, though its exact legal basis is unclear (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). A pending Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) would create a new Annex XIV listing notified/designated organizations within the NANDO system (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)). For comparison, as of October 2025 NANDO listed 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies under separate medical device regulations, not the AI Act (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources disagree on whether Annex VII assessment is strictly mandatory for biometric systems or conditional on standards application (**flagged**: both sources below 0.4 confidence) ([Quantamix](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment) vs. [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)). Sources also conflict on designation timing: one states that no notified bodies had been designated under the AI Act for medical-device-related high-risk systems as of April 2026, while another frames notified-body assessments as a "post-2026" event without clarifying whether any designations had already occurred at the time of its publication, creating ambiguity about whether any AI Act-specific notified bodies exist yet (**flagged**: both sources below 0.4 confidence) ([AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide) vs. [MDXCRO](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd)). Several low-confidence claims (0.03–0.17) rely on undated blog sources rather than primary legal text, including claims about Article 43(5) delegated acts for updating Annexes VI and VII, sourced to the [FPF Working Paper](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf), and claims about Article 35's requirements for identification numbers and public lists of notified bodies, sourced to [regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35).

## Knowledge Gaps
No source provides a verifiable list of named organizations designated as AI Act notified bodies. It remains unclear whether any designations occurred between April 2026 and the October 2026 question date. The relationship between existing MDR/IVDR notified bodies and new AI Act-specific designations for medical AI remains unresolved. Whether COM(2025) 836's proposed Annex XIV has been adopted is unknown. No data exists on notified body capacity, geographic distribution, or assessment wait times under the AI Act specifically.

# Conformity Assessment for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act: Procedures and Notified Body Designation Status

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes a dual-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems: internal control (Annex VI) or notified body assessment (Annex VII), with the latter generally mandatory for biometric identification systems and products already subject to sectoral safety legislation (medium confidence). However, the notified body ecosystem required to implement Annex VII assessments appears largely undeveloped, with no source identifying specific organizations designated under the AI Act itself as of early-to-mid 2026, despite the approaching August 2026 deadline for high-risk obligations (low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 of the AI Act establishes two primary routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)). For biometric identification systems under Annex III point 1, providers may use internal control if harmonised standards or common specifications were applied, but must use the notified body procedure under Annex VII where standards were not fully applied (low confidence) ([EC Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf)). Interpretive sources suggest Annex VII is effectively mandatory for biometric systems and for high-risk AI embedded as safety components in products covered by Annex I Section A legislation, with most other high-risk systems eligible for Annex VI self-assessment (low confidence) ([Quantamix](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)).

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU product-safety legislation (e.g., medical devices, machinery) under Annex I Section A, providers must follow that sectoral legislation's conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI-specific compliance (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

### Procedural Details
A new conformity assessment is required after substantial modification, unless changes were predetermined and documented at initial assessment—relevant to continuously learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Under Article 43(1), providers may generally choose any notified body, except where systems are intended for use by law enforcement, immigration/asylum authorities, or EU institutions, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from standard assessment for limited periods on public security or health grounds (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Annex VII point 4.5 allows notified bodies access to training and trained models, including parameters, where necessary and subject to IP/confidentiality protections (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing across Member States and uncertain capacity ahead of the August 2026 deadline (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)). As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated for medical-device-related high-risk AI systems specifically (low confidence) ([AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)). A Council document (ST-7322-2026) describes a coding system (e.g., AIP 0101) for defining designation scope tied to Annex I categories, though its exact legal basis is unclear (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). A pending Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) would create a new Annex XIV listing notified/designated organizations within the NANDO system (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)). For comparison, as of October 2025 NANDO listed 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies under separate medical device regulations, not the AI Act (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources disagree on whether Annex VII assessment is strictly mandatory for biometric systems or conditional on standards application (**flagged**: both sources below 0.4 confidence) ([Quantamix](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment) vs. [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)). Sources also conflict on designation timing: one states no AI Act notified bodies existed by April 2026, while another frames designation as a future event without clarifying status (both low confidence). Several low-confidence claims (0.03–0.17) rely on undated blog sources rather than primary legal text, including claims about Article 43(5) delegated acts and Article 35 identification numbers.

## Knowledge Gaps
No source provides a verifiable list of named organizations designated as AI Act notified bodies. It remains unclear whether any designations occurred between April 2026 and the October 2026 question date. The relationship between existing MDR/IVDR notified bodies and new AI Act-specific designations for medical AI remains unresolved. Whether COM(2025) 836's proposed Annex XIV has been adopted is unknown. No data exists on notified body capacity, geographic distribution, or assessment wait times under the AI Act specifically.
